issues.description: GKE detection by name-prefix 'gke-' is a brittle heuristic and trivially bypassable.
issues.detail: Using instance.name.startswith('gke-') to grant MANUAL status conflates a string identity with the fact 'managed by GKE.' Any user can name a VM 'gke-foo' to evade the check; legitimate GKE nodes with custom prefixes get FAIL. Use a real signal: instance labels (goog-gke-node), metadata keys, or MIG membership.

issues.description: Check name, metadata, CHANGELOG, and tri-state code disagree on what the check reports.
issues.detail: PR title and CHANGELOG describe detecting 'multiple network interfaces' (PASS/FAIL), but the directory, class, and CheckID use 'single_network_interface' and the code emits a third MANUAL state not documented in metadata.json or the PR description. Reconcile naming and document MANUAL, or drop the GKE branch.

issues.description: Zero-interface branch silently PASSes, is untested, and contradicts the semantic intent.
issues.detail: When interface_count == 0 the report stays PASS with a 'has no network interfaces' message. A VM with zero NICs is anomalous, not compliant, and no test exercises this branch. Either remove the branch, FAIL/MANUAL explicitly, or document why PASS is correct and add a test.

issues.description: NetworkInterface value model drops the fields needed to distinguish real cross-boundary bridges.
issues.detail: The parsed model keeps only {name, network, subnetwork} via split('/')[-1], discarding accessConfigs/natIP, full network URL, alias IP ranges, and stack type. Two NICs with same short name in different projects (shared VPC) collide. Keep the richer value so the check can ask the interesting question.

issues.description: Mutable default '[]' on Pydantic network_interfaces field is fragile and inconsistent.
issues.detail: network_interfaces: list[NetworkInterface] = [] reads as a Python mutable-default footgun. Pydantic v1 copies per-instance, but the idiom is fragile against version changes. Prefer Field(default_factory=list) and match surrounding codebase style.

issues.description: interface_names computed unconditionally even when unused by the PASS/zero branches.
issues.detail: Line 22-24 builds interface_names for every instance including the single-NIC PASS path that only references index [0] and the zero-interface branch that doesn't use it. Move the list-comprehension inside the FAIL branch that actually uses it for cleaner reading.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the check works and is tested but ships with three blocking issues and several taste-grade concerns. The GKE exemption via name-prefix 'gke-' is unanimously flagged as a brittle, bypassable heuristic that should use labels or MIG membership instead. Naming and state semantics disagree across PR title, CHANGELOG, metadata, and code (which emits an undocumented MANUAL state). The zero-interface branch silently PASSes without a test. Secondary concerns: the NetworkInterface model strips fields needed to detect real cross-boundary bridges, a mutable Pydantic default, and unconditional computation of interface_names. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK before merge.
